ranking.note: Right buyer finally (defense lawyers with standing, deadline, fee-shifting); defect patterns feed class-action data. $99 audits are tiny and unauthorized-practice risk remains.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Data-pooling cold start and antitrust exposure; payers must adopt index.
ranking.note: Neutral implant reference index could end invoice-attachment fights; ratio-only design is clever. Pooling cold start, antitrust, and PHI make it a slow standard-setting bet.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Leakage may be under 2%; Aspirion could add carve-outs; commercial contracts only.
ranking.note: Biller-channel and switch-moment lookback is smart distribution, but leakage may be small at specialist billers and each payer contract needs hand reading.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection, licensing, and capital needs; NextGear/Cox can undercut.
ranking.note: Reframing sold-out-of-trust as a timing gap is sharp, but it is a capital-heavy lending business with adverse selection and state licensing.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection; vets refuse to police clients; government reporting substitutes.
ranking.note: Bundling two vet-dependent products compounds risk: borrower-initiated audits suffer adverse selection, and selling outbreak signals to funds raises MNPI concerns.

ranking.fatal_flaw: FHA needs easement not maintenance agreement; association layer costs more than PayHOA.
ranking.note: Neighbor-consent workflow is the real insight, but FHA premise is weaker than stated and per-deal fees ($495) cap the prize.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Weak legal value without enforceable IP; cheap tier crowded by ImportGenius.
ranking.note: Customs-trail forensics for off-book tooling overruns is useful, but ImportGenius occupies the cheap tier and evidence matters only when IP is enforceable in China.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Lapse is not death; underwriters may reject memos; unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure.
ranking.note: Zombie-lien proof-of-death is a real title pain, but lapse does not clear leases, debtor-filed terminations are narrow, and underwriters may refuse memos.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Cold-start pooling, PBM confidentiality clauses, antitrust; cannot be built before January.
ranking.note: Two-sided data pooling with employers is the harder, riskier version; confidentiality, antitrust, and the January window undermine it. Mutation M1 is better.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Remote arrestee clearance liability may be uninsurable; small county ACV, slow sales.
ranking.note: Bundle doubles clinical liability for thin revenue: remote jail clearance shifts head-injury risk to vendor, and ACV is about $5k a month.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Premise overstated: no add-on deadline in statute; BHPH dealers have no lender cascade.
ranking.note: Timely California SB 766 hook, but statute imposes no add-on cancellation deadline, dealers already run unwinds, and credit unions gain no direct economics.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Own numbers show cost of $4-5k per resident exceeds the $1.8-3.5k price.
ranking.note: Unit economics break at 6-15 residents per two-aide shift, and licensing is fragile where service bundles resemble assisted living. Aging-in-place is a crowded thesis.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Lender has no incentive; success fee on member refund is bad optics.
ranking.note: Credit union gets no economic benefit from member refunds, success-fee optics are poor, sales cycle is slow, and the SB 766 citation failed to verify.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Four free competitors; payment-standard timing premise is wrong.
ranking.note: Reminder layer already served by free tools; two clocks conflated (payment standard applies at reexam), rent reasonableness caps gains; tiny market.

ranking.fatal_flaw: none
ranking.note: Information gap (nobody tells the administrator the loan ended) plus contingency pricing gives low-friction entry; the loan-end event dataset is a real exchange asset.

ranking.fatal_flaw: No legal mandate to buy a registry filing; adoption depends on slow ordinances and legislation.
ranking.note: Neutral notary for tamper-evident baselines sits on top of data-center backlash; incumbents become channel. Huge upside if one county or statute names it.

ranking.fatal_flaw: none
ranking.note: Inverts the archive-mining thesis: measure fresh gas with pumpers as sensors; operators already pay for assays. Odd, cheap, proprietary labels for a funded sector.

ranking.fatal_flaw: none
ranking.note: Selling regulator acceptance, not models, in a fresh rule window with reusable HIL-validated platform models; needs scarce power-electronics talent and OEM NDAs.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Federal emergency-engine rules bar capacity revenue without costly reclassification and Tier 4 retrofits.
ranking.note: Biggest prize in batch: capacity already built, blocked by permits. Genuine seam, but the data-center power theme is crowded and operators resist running gensets.

ranking.fatal_flaw: IFR limits plans to assisting only; state verification tools may make a separate packet redundant.
ranking.note: Hard Jan 2027 deadline and MCOs/FQHCs with real revenue at stake; enrollee-side documentation for gig and cash work is unaddressed; policy risk high.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Brokers may refuse to pay $1.5k+ per listing; permit transferability wedge is thin.
ranking.note: Tangible physical-world insight: energized service, permits and cranes are the real asset, and data centers compete for the same shells. Verified-building data is unusual.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Anonymity leaks in small subfields; postdoc confidentiality and defamation exposure; GLG can copy.
ranking.note: Right insight: candid junior-bench consensus beats conflicted KOL calls; cheap to start, $5k polls. Small market and weak why-now beyond layoffs.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Leaks are rare, so attestations mostly say 'nothing found'; vendors may object to enrolments.
ranking.note: Honeytokens applied to ID verifiers is original and timed to IDScan and EU age-check wave. Buyers want protection, not proof; evidence is probabilistic.

ranking.fatal_flaw: CMS or wholesalers could shorten refund timing, deleting the float within quarters.
ranking.note: Policy-lag bridge financing on a statutory refund stream, sharpened to large-float LTC pharmacies. Real money, but capital-heavy, window short, wholesalers hold the payment path.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Requires lenders to change funding conditions; loan-financed solar volume is shrinking after 25D ended.
ranking.note: Sharp insight: the lender already holds the cure budget (final milestone) and controls deposits. Strong pre-failure positioning, but installer CRMs and lenders could build it.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Weak defensibility; QoE firms or M&A lawyers can bundle it, and deal volume is small.
ranking.note: Sells to the buyer at peak willingness to pay; findings convert directly to closing conditions or price cuts. Fast to launch, modest ceiling.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Tiny Japan-only niche; franchise agreements may bar third-party data tools; asymmetry fades post-2027.
ranking.note: Sharp payoff-transform insight: back out HQ AI's implied quantile and re-apply the owner's contract payoff. Prize and market size are small.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Issuer-pays conflict undermines credibility; regulatory risk if rate cards read as justifying inflated bills.
ranking.note: Smart inversion: subpoena as fear purchase, clinic ledgers as proprietary realized-value data. Credibility and ethics are shaky; Florida statute shrinks the benchmark gap.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Per-case revenue is tiny and credit-linked loans add risk; Kenya-specific execution needed.
ranking.note: SACCOs own payroll check-off and a stuck-deposit liability, making milestone escrow plausible. Original frontier-market structure, but dollar prize small and SACCO sales cycles slow.

ranking.fatal_flaw: ImportGenius already sells supplier verification at same price; records often name forwarders, not factories.
ranking.note: Strong why-now in transshipment enforcement, but the wedge is thin: data incumbents can add a risk report, and the factory-pays credential is unproven.

ranking.fatal_flaw: California appeal right appears not enacted; Colorado law may not require insurers to accept imagery.
ranking.note: Real 30 m vs 30 cm resolution insight, but only Colorado confirmed, free kits cap price, imagery vendors hold same data.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Tiny, shrinking TAM at $695 one-time; insurers' free tails reduce urgency.
ranking.note: Notary-not-storage framing is clever and sellable fast, with UAD 3.6 exit wave as trigger. One-time fees and a niche ceiling cap the prize.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Statute does not require add-on cancellation within 48 hours; dealers already unwind deals; volume small.
ranking.note: Timely new law and data angle, but premise undercut: deductions are formulaic, lender lag excused, return volume per dealer tiny.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Florida statute and free CMS data let carriers copy the benchmark cheaply; Enlyte nearby.
ranking.note: Coder bench with cross-examination-proof methodology is a real gap, but low price points, commodity inputs and mismatched why-now make it copyable.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Retail B2C estates at about $200 each; Advocates Act and diaspora willingness unproven.
ranking.note: Cohort density per chief's location is a real insight, but consumer WhatsApp sales and tiny tickets make it a slog; SACCO sibling distributes better.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Free-rider households and lending or money-transmission licensing; small early revenue; Jobber-type tools could copy.
ranking.note: Contractor-as-customer is a smarter wedge than formation, and the entity becomes collateral. Still a small rural niche; the lending upside is speculative.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Maine-only, attorney-dependent; about $60k year-one revenue and low turnover cap the business.
ranking.note: Careful RESPA-aware design and a resale toll are neat, but a statute-patching local service is a lifestyle business, not a world-beater.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Slow bank adoption; borrower rider and third-party record access may be contested.
ranking.note: Count the paper, not cattle: covenant-funded reconciliation from third-party records fixes adverse selection; record cattle prices and fraud losses give lenders budget and urgency.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Needs verified-human control panel; building or licensing one is slow and costly.
ranking.note: Buyer-side referee with ground-truth humans is genuinely non-obvious as agents defeat attention checks; calibration, not detection, is the gap. Vendors cannot referee themselves.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Rulings bind only addressee and identical goods; Section 232 list changes can undo redesigns.
ranking.note: Design-stage tariff engineering plus binding rulings is a real, unpackaged mid-market gap with large rate spreads and fast fixed-fee cash.

ranking.fatal_flaw: SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek already sell sampling and umpire assay; black mass handling is hazmat.
ranking.note: Mining sampling theory imported into a chemist-run scrap trade is sharp and non-obvious; niche prize, and incumbents may claim they already do it.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Chicken-and-egg: certificates from one shop's invoices carry little weight before an index exists.
ranking.note: Becoming the named reference in contracts is the durable PRA moat; tariff-driven escalation disputes give a dated pain and a certificate wedge.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Needs critical mass of contributing pharmacies; antitrust and PBM-contract confidentiality exposure.
ranking.note: Neutral index cited in statutes is a standards play timed to 2027 sessions; association evidence packs give early cash, but data cold-start is slow.

ranking.fatal_flaw: State procurement cycles; Maximus-type vendors can bundle training; modest roughly $10-20M ceiling.
ranking.note: Deadline-driven by H.R.1 error-rate cost shares; recall loop on states' own QC findings is a smart data position, but small, slow government buyers.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Listing-vanish signal is noisy and misses Tricolor-style double-pledged loan collateral.
ranking.note: Selling verification to the lender's lender, paid via facility fees, is a smart payer inversion after Tricolor; sticky covenant revenue if the signal proves precise.

ranking.fatal_flaw: State manager-in-charge rules may block 24-48 hour interim coverage; adverse selection, liability.
ranking.note: Genuinely out-of-the-box: owner's license is a single point of failure, and succession pipeline is clever, but small prize and unverified legality.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Commissioning firms already load-test; insurer capacity and MGA licensing make the wrap slow.
ranking.note: Beats its parent: neutral cross-vendor failure data could price post-warranty risk for lenders, but the test phase is commissioning and the moat accrues slowly.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer set; tariffs and collateral rules make applicants self-prove, shrinking the desk's role.
ranking.note: Applicant-paid gates and parcel-keyed duplicate registry are sharper than the original, but co-op G&T market is small and regulators are eating the problem.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Existing hospital Medicaid-eligibility outsourcers can add informal-income evidence; weak defensibility.
ranking.note: Hard January 2027 retro-coverage cut makes speed a priced variable and pay-on-approval removes buyer risk, but it's a services wedge into an entrenched field.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive; consumer-lending licensing and FTC Holder Rule liability exceed a scrappy team.
ranking.note: Inverting from fee to ownership captures the cure uplift, contrarian and well-timed after installer bankruptcies, but needs balance sheet and the cure-share phase is thin.

ranking.fatal_flaw: States may verify placement from wage records; SIS vendors can bolt it on.
ranking.note: Hybrid fixes pay-app cold start with a compliance-driven school wedge, but the market is small, three-sided, and driver stub uploads will lag.

ranking.fatal_flaw: County-by-county recorder image access unproven; developers may not record options before announcing.
ranking.note: Join of land, permit and queue data is clever, but bigger and more diffuse than the sharper intake-desk sibling; hybrid isn't clearly stronger.

ranking.fatal_flaw: IEP Advocate.ai sells this at $30/mo; free ChatGPT covers most of it.
ranking.note: Service-minute ledger and procedural-pressure insight are real and sympathetic, but it's an AI legal-wrapper with consumer churn once disputes end.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; carriers may not fund loss control before any AI-exclusion claims exist.
ranking.note: Payer inversion to E&O carriers who pay regardless of duty is clever, but speculative demand, slow carrier procurement, and a free-tracker-crowded exclusion niche.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Carriers need not accept the format; standards need carrier adoption before contractors see value.
ranking.note: Signed-capture provenance for mitigation evidence fits the AI-faked-photo era, but it's a standards play with chicken-and-egg adoption and thin per-job revenue.

ranking.fatal_flaw: QoE boutiques can add materials reconciliation; small deal volume caps the prize.
ranking.note: Changing payer to acquirers fixes the parent's flaws and sells fast, but it is a thin copyable diligence add-on with a small market.

ranking.fatal_flaw: California-only court procurement, ruling-dependent demand, reporter-union opposition; courts may build intake in-house.
ranking.note: Fixes the parent's illegal remote-reporting mechanic and outcome pricing is clever, but it is a narrow, slow government services bet on one ruling.

ranking.fatal_flaw: DJI/CarePro and Drone Nerds already repair; DJI parts access and battery lockouts cap moat.
ranking.note: Serving the stranded installed base is sensible and easy to start, but it is commodity repair with no moat and incumbents already serve it.

ranking.fatal_flaw: TrueLoad sells software load calcs at $30; a $79-149 stamped premium is thin and copyable.
ranking.note: Panel capacity as the electrification bottleneck is a fair insight, but it's a small-ticket desk job with solar engineering desks able to add the SKU.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Contingency claims are hard to collect; clocks mostly start at startup, narrowing exposure.
ranking.note: Silent-expiry warranty clock is a neat observation, but OEMs can deny on storage grounds, recovery is hard to measure, and the offspring supersedes it.

ranking.note: Utilization insight is good but the core mechanic is illegal in California courts; the Record-on-Request offspring replaces it.

ranking.fatal_flaw: State contractor licensing and lenders' existing in-house step-in crews may shrink the buyer pool.
ranking.note: Stranded solar is a records and legal-standing problem, not labor. Lender pays, hard Freedom Forever clock, tens of thousands of dark systems. Strongest why-now and buyer.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Cold-start consortium; CMS speeding refunds would shrink the float and lender demand.
ranking.note: New statutory-refund asset class with no data owner. Credit-bureau inversion is original, float is large, standard files make a small-team build credible.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Slow county adoption; neutral trustee takes liability exposure and needs credible hydrogeology.
ranking.note: Sells the legal instrument, not sensors. County attorney as real buyer removes the developer's admission problem. Live permit politics make a template spreadable.

ranking.fatal_flaw: States own training; county budgets thin; per-state case libraries costly to maintain.
ranking.note: Hard H.R.1 clock, buyers in pain now, and synthetic cases dodge PII and security review so selling starts in weeks. Govtech speed is the risk.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Small buyer pool; battery repair fire liability; estate parts may already be sold.
ranking.note: Military orphan-platform sustainment imported to failed EV makers is a fresh insight. Pooled spares math is real, and every EV bankruptcy widens the base.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Reserve pool paying claims is unlicensed insurance; early fees tiny per dairy.
ranking.note: Warranty by the party controlling the risk flips moral hazard; beef-on-dairy boom makes calves valuable. Original, but slow-building and structurally regulated.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Credits owed may be small; no proof vendors concede claims; assumptions unverified.
ranking.note: Contingency audit starting with already-conceded credits gives cash in weeks with no dispute. Practical and feasible; insight is a vertical transplant of freight audit.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Neutrality unproven across three sides; labor-heavy; incumbent auditors could rebrand within quarters.
ranking.note: Selling the measured disagreement rate is clever; every incumbent becomes a customer, and contested-encounter files can pay early. Credibility is slow to build.

ranking.note: Collateral rules create a substitute market needing a readiness underwriter. Sharp insight, big upside if bonds work, but multi-party chicken-and-egg within six months.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Operators reluctant to share facility data; OEM and PQ-meter vendors can add analytics.
ranking.note: Better than parent: software-first, ingests data sites already log, neutral cross-vendor network is a real cornered resource. Still a hot, crowded theme.

ranking.note: Systematic bias, not noise, is the non-obvious insight; euro-quantified free historical-pair test makes outbound sales concrete. Prize is small and niche.

ranking.note: Notification law turns on data, not credentials: sharp reframing with real incident volume. Sold through IR boutiques, but proof gap and easy copying cap it.

ranking.note: Tacit acceptance rules and the human decider are the real data, which registries miss. RHTP money helps, but voice-agent core is a known pattern.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure; state-by-state drafting; modest total market.

ranking.fatal_flaw: No vet contracts; line reductions fall on policyholders, inviting complaints and regulators.
ranking.note: Claim edits before AI is a good insight and a free retrospective is an easy sale. But no pet-insurer demand evidence and small per-claim prize.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Small utilities have little budget to act; speculative buyer demand for dead plants.
ranking.note: Utility holds the meter data and will-serve letter, an unusual buyer choice. But rate-impact premise is unvalidated and the buyer pool is thin.

ranking.note: Tool as the only expensive asset that reports nothing is a neat inversion. But hardware, molder cooperation and a speculative registry standard make it slow.

ranking.note: Compliance-budget twist on the same sampling insight, but depends on an unverified reading of the delegated act. Smaller prize and weaker pull than sibling M1.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Contractor warranty-gap exposure is unvalidated; OEM deferral riders already exist.
ranking.note: Contractor squeezed between two warranty clocks is a clever reframing, with a CFO-owned budget. But the reserve size is assumed and construction sales are slow.

ranking.fatal_flaw: About 0.5% hit rate; regulators unlikely to approve liability transfer to thin juniors.
ranking.note: Wrong-sign bid-ask spread on idle wells is an original reframing. But economics barely cover screening cost and the transfer playbook is heavy regulatory work.

ranking.note: Parametric neighbor payout is interesting but sold on top of a crowded sensor business. The sharpened M1 version dominates this original.

ranking.fatal_flaw: Free ISO/EPRI models, OEM-held controls, and HIL-lab dependence undercut a consulting model.
ranking.note: Data center as grid device is now a consensus AI-power second-order idea; services-heavy, model library commoditizable. Offspring M3 is stronger.
